eligibility_reason: Original research proposing SAMF-YOLO (based on YOLOv11s) and evaluating it on NEU-DET (Table 7).

F01.evidence: NEU-DET focuses specifically on steel surface defects, containing 1,800 grayscale images classified into six typical defect categories: crazing, patches, inclusion, pitted surface, rolled-in scale, and scratches.

F02.evidence: Additionally, to improve the consistency of training and evaluation, the datasets were split into 70% for training, 20% for validation, and 10% for testing.

F05.location: full text (self-supervised contrastive learning is described for UniRepLKNet, but pretrained weight initialization for NEU-DET and baselines is not specified)

F09.evidence: All images were resized to 640×640 before being fed into the model to maintain consistency and reduce computational load.

F14.evidence: Detailed hyper-parameters listed in Table 2 were uniformly used across all models evaluated, ensuring fairness and consistency throughout the experimental comparisons.

F15.value: NVIDIA RTX 4080 Super (16 GB) reported; batch size, precision, and pre/post-processing for FPS not reported
